rationale: Modern game agents (e.g., self-play trained value/policy networks) literally induce general positional principles and pattern regularities from vast experience and generalize them to unseen states, though the induction is confined to a closed, fully-specified rule world rather than noisy real-world evidence.

Game-playing agents perform arithmetic only internally (position evaluation, score aggregation) and are not built to take arithmetic inputs and return computed sums, products or quotients, so support for the ability's core calculation tasks is incidental rather than direct.

Game engines rapidly compare huge numbers of board states, detect transpositions and matching patterns, and evaluate positional similarities far faster and more accurately than humans, which covers the core comparison sub-tasks; it falls slightly short only because the ability is framed around visual comparison of symbolic/pictorial material rather than internal state representations.

Rate control is a continuous psychomotor timing skill requiring perception of moving objects and real-time motor adjustment, whereas abstract strategy game agents operate on discrete, static, turn-based state spaces with no motion tracking or motor output.
A board-game search agent produces discrete move selections with no physical embodiment or motor control, so it contributes nothing to repeated bending, stretching, or twisting of the body.

The agent acts through digital control signals in a simulated environment and has no physical arm or hand, so it contributes nothing to stabilizing real limb position; the only faint link is precise continuous control of a virtual cursor/aim, which is not the physical ability.

Game-playing agents literally perform choice-reaction: mapping distinct perceptual signals to distinct discrete actions with minimal latency, which is the computational core of response orientation; the discount reflects that the ability is defined over physical movement selection, which the agent only emulates via virtual controls.

Glare sensitivity is a physiological property of human vision under real-world bright-light conditions; a game agent reads clean rendered frames or game state and never contends with optical glare, mirroring the 0.00 given to Far Vision.

Game-playing agents act primarily on visual/state input and, even when audio channels exist, the measured competence is control policy quality rather than detecting or discriminating pitch and loudness; FRS scores perceptual abilities outside the visual-action loop (e.g., Far Vision) at 0.

Game-playing agents act on visual or state observations under time pressure; segregating a target sound stream from competing auditory distractors is not part of their pipeline, and FRS scored even sensory vision abilities at 0.00 for this application.

Object labelling in still images produces category tags, not comprehension of written prose; any link runs only through adjacent OCR-style text detection, which is outside this application's defined scope of categorising visual objects.

Image classification applies learned category boundaries to specific instances, which superficially resembles applying general rules to particular cases, but it is pattern matching over pixels rather than chained inference from stated premises, so it supports only the perceptual front-end of deductive tasks.

Image recognition labels static images and does not itself shift between tasks or information streams; it only indirectly supports time sharing by automating parallel visual monitoring (e.g., several camera feeds) so a person need not switch attention among them.

Finger dexterity is a fine motor manipulation ability requiring physical actuation and haptic feedback; a still-image labeling model produces no motor output, matching the near-zero calibration for other manual abilities like arm-hand steadiness and wrist-finger speed.

Control precision is a psychomotor ability requiring continuous fine motor actuation of controls; a still-image labeling model produces category outputs and cannot execute or regulate any adjustment, offering at most incidental visual feedback that would need a separate control system.

Speed of Closure is a visual pattern-integration ability " quickly recognizing meaningful configurations from degraded or cluttered imagery " which is exactly what a VQA model's perception stack performs when it parses a scene and answers a question about it; it falls slightly short of the perfect scores given to elementary visual abilities because rapid gestalt completion from heavily incomplete or ambiguous input remains a common failure mode.

VQA can answer questions about relative object positions and viewpoint-referenced layout from an image, covering the perceptual judgement half of spatial orientation, but it operates on static single images without the continuous egocentric self-localization and movement-through-environment component the ability centers on.

VQA grounds spatial relations and object configurations in an image and can answer some transformation questions verbally, but it perceives a given scene rather than simulating how parts would look after rearrangement or rotation, which is the ability's core; mental-rotation-style queries are a known failure mode.
Multilimb coordination is a purely psychomotor ability requiring physical actuation of limbs; a model that answers questions about images provides no motor control or physical execution.

Static strength is a purely physical force-exertion ability requiring a body; a multimodal model answering questions about images provides no force output and does not substitute for any lifting, pushing, or carrying sub-task.

Perceptual speed is a discriminative task—rapidly matching and spotting differences across sets of symbols or images—whereas an image generator only synthesises new outputs and offers no comparison or verification interface, giving at best incidental support through its learned visual similarity representations.
Image synthesis produces pixels from prompts and involves no physical grasping, manipulation or assembly, so it cannot substitute for or assist hand-arm motor execution.
Image synthesis produces visual outputs and exerts no physical force, so it cannot perform or assist any lifting, pushing, pulling, or carrying task.
Image synthesis produces static visual artefacts and has no bearing on whole-body motor control, which requires physical execution and real-time proprioceptive feedback.

Image synthesis requires internal color composition and fidelity to color descriptions, which indirectly touches color handling, but the ability's core task is perceptual matching and detection of subtle shade/brightness differences in existing stimuli \u2014 a discriminative input task the generative model is not built to perform.

The semantic understanding half of oral comprehension is exactly what this system does, but the defining input modality
i.e. listening to speech, with its prosody, disfluency, accents and real-time flow
is absent since the application only reads supplied text; it helps only via a transcript intermediary.

Reading comprehension operates purely on text input and produces textual answers; it provides no motor control, physical manipulation, or sensorimotor feedback needed for grasping and assembling objects.
Reading comprehension operates purely on text inputs and produces textual answers, offering nothing for physical coordination of limbs, which requires motor control and embodiment.
Extent Flexibility is a purely physical range-of-motion ability with no textual inputs or outputs; a text-reading QA model cannot perform or assist any of its core tasks.

Reading comprehension operates on already-supplied digital text and involves no visual sensing or resolution of fine detail at close range; the perceptual acquisition step is entirely outside the application.

Multilimb coordination is a purely psychomotor ability requiring physical actuation and real-time sensorimotor feedback; a text-predicting model has no effectors and cannot perform any of its core tasks.

Response Orientation is a psychomotor ability requiring rapid perceptual-motor choice and physical movement initiation; a text-predicting model has no sensorimotor loop or effectors and cannot execute any of its core tasks.
Static strength is a purely physical exertion capacity requiring a body; a text-predicting model has no actuators and cannot lift, push, or carry anything.
Stamina is a purely cardiorespiratory physical capacity; a text-predicting model cannot exert physical effort or substitute for aerobic endurance in any core sub-task.
Far Vision is a purely perceptual, physical sensing ability at distance; a text-only language model has no visual input or optical acuity and cannot perform any of its core tasks.

A translation model must sometimes find inventive equivalents for idioms, puns and register, which is a narrow slice of creative problem-solving, but its objective is fidelity to a source text rather than generating novel ideas about a topic or situation.

Translation models operate on symbolic text and can implicitly align and match source-target strings, which touches pattern comparison, but rapid visual discrimination among letters, numbers, objects or pictures is not a core sub-task of a text-to-text translation model.
Translation is a text-to-text linguistic model with no motor output or physical actuation, so it cannot perform or assist rapid repetitive finger and wrist movements.

Text translation operates on already-digitized text and does not perform close-range visual detail perception; any link is incidental (e.g., reading source documents), not a core capability of the translation model.

The measured model is text-to-text, so it does not itself perform acoustic decoding of speech; it only supports understanding spoken input indirectly when paired with a transcription front end, though speech-translation pipelines make this adjacency common (cf. Oral Comprehension at 0.50).
Speech recognition maps acoustic signals to text and provides no spatial or visual representation, so it contributes nothing to mentally transforming or rearranging objects.
Speech-to-text transcription operates on audio signals and produces text; it has no motor or physical stabilization component and cannot perform any part of steadying an arm or hand.
Speech recognition transcribes audio to text and has no bearing on physical exertion or muscular endurance, which requires bodily force output.
Speech-to-text transcription operates entirely on audio signals and produces text; it has no bearing on generating physical muscular force or propulsion.

Speech recognition transcribes audio to text and has no bearing on cardiovascular endurance or sustained physical exertion, which requires bodily capacity rather than any information processing output.

Multilimb coordination is a purely physical psychomotor ability requiring embodied control of limbs; an agent operating in digital environments has no body and cannot execute or substitute for any of its core tasks.

Response Orientation is a psychomotor speed ability requiring rapid selection among physical movements in response to sensory signals; agentic task execution operates purely in digital environments with no motor response channel, and its latency profile (deliberate multi-step planning) is unrelated to reaction-time performance.

Peripheral vision is an embodied visual-field ability tied to physical gaze and detecting off-axis motion; an agent operating in a digital environment has no eyes, no visual field, and no core tasks that decompose into this perceptual capacity.

Agentic execution operates on text, code, and GUI/browser state; selectively attending to one sound stream amid competing audio is not a modality the scaffolding acts on, and any speech-transcription overlap is incidental rather than core.

Speech Clarity concerns intelligible vocal articulation, a physical/audio production skill outside the defined scope of an agent that browses, calls APIs, operates software and runs code; at most it touches it indirectly if a voice interface is bolted on.

Formal derivation can substitute for some spatial tasks (geometry, stereochemistry, transformation problems) by converting them to symbolic/coordinate reasoning, but the application's core is multi-step formal inference rather than imagining rearranged objects, and it lacks reliable visuospatial imagery.
Arm-hand steadiness is a purely physical motor-control ability requiring a body; a formal reasoning system produces symbolic derivations and has no actuation or physical stabilization capacity.
Night vision is a low-light visual perception capability; a symbolic multi-step reasoning system engages no visual sensing and contributes nothing to seeing in darkness.

Glare sensitivity is a low-level visual perceptual capacity dependent on the eye's optics and physical light conditions; a formal reasoning system produces no perceptual input or output relevant to it.
Formal derivation from text-based problem statements involves no audio perception or comprehension of spoken language; speech recognition is a separate modality not engaged by this application.

The application's core loop is text-based (issue text, code, tests) with no speech input; spoken-language understanding is not a modality it operates in, though the underlying language comprehension it demonstrates is adjacent to and could be paired with transcription.

Speed of Closure is a perceptual gestalt ability (recognizing a pattern from incomplete or degraded stimuli), which is not core to patching code; the coding agent does synthesize scattered repository information into a coherent model of a bug, which is a loose analogue, but the perceptual modality the ability actually measures is absent — consistent with the 0.00 given to Perceptual Speed.
Software engineering AI produces code patches from text inputs and has no physical actuation or object manipulation, so it cannot perform any grasping or assembly sub-tasks.
Resolving code issues and writing patches involves no perception of distant physical detail; the application operates entirely on text within a codebase.

The application operates purely on text artifacts (issues, source code, test output) and involves no audio input or spoken-language understanding, so it contributes essentially nothing to identifying and comprehending another person's speech.
